rv.q: As an experience to just wash over you and let the moments that strike you strike you, The Kick Inside has its pleasures.

But the production never quite converts its fragments into a larger experience, and its apparent refusal to make connections eventually becomes less an aesthetic provocation than an artistic limitation.
This is live theater at its absolute best.
The Kick Inside serves as a time capsule, catapulting its audiences back to the heyday of experimental theater.
The Kick Inside feels completely random; it has aliens, a talking canine, milkshakes, and innards.

cn.t: An experimental throwback to '60s avant-garde theater divides critics: some praise its ambitious non-linear vignettes and steady direction, while others find its randomness and obscurity more frustrating than rewarding.
